articles.title: Hazel (YC W24) Is Hiring for Our Largest Government Contract
articles.originalTitle: Hazel (YC W24) Is Hiring for Our Largest Government Contract
articles.excerpt:
Note: This role is exclusively available to U.S. citizens who can obtain and maintain a U.S. government-issued Top
Secret security clearance with full-scope polygraph. There are no exceptions.

Who We Are:

Our mission at Hazel is simple and powerful. We use AI to help U.S. government purchasing teams buy at the speed of need
with unparalleled efficiency and cost-effectiveness. It is a $2.7T problem every single year, and Hazel is at the
forefront with Federal and State, Local, and EDucation (SLED) agencies.  

Hazel has identified a once-in-a-lifetime opportunity to solve this by deploying cutting-edge AI to the public sector
and unlocking the full potential of our nation. We empower our partners to move with expediency against the most
pressing challenges of this century. Hazel builds AI for the public interest.

What We Are Building:

Hazel is transforming government procurement: how government agencies purchase goods and services from commercial
vendors. You’ll work directly with our federal partners in deploying our AI-forward bid evaluations solution, helping
them assess vendors more accurately, reliably, and quickly. With the federal government under increasing pressure to
accelerate acquisitions, our tools give them a real edge.

Our full COTS platform supports the entire procurement lifecycle from need identification through award management, and
our other partners include state & local governments, schools, and special authorities.

About the Role:

As a Hazel full stack engineer, you will be at the helm of architecting and building Hazel’s platform. You will work
closely with Hazel’s customers to identify pain points to prioritize the most impactful features.  You will build new
features every week and be faced with many challenging technical problems. Most importantly, you join the tip of the
spear in delivering effective and secure AI for the public sector.

This specific role is for deploying and scaling Hazel's cutting-edge AI for our largest contract with one of the most
important U.S. government agencies. You will bring it into production by owning the customization, security
accreditation, and deployment of Hazel in a unique operational environment. 

What You’ll Do Day-to-Day:

  - Define, iterate, and execute on projects contributing to Hazel’s federal and commercial product roadmap 
  - Identify areas for process and technical improvements, and take the initiative to enhance engineering processes and
    structures in classified environments 
  - Collaborate with colleagues, customers, and partners to understand key tactical and strategic priorities and deliver
    innovative, impactful solutions 
  - Take ownership of projects, ensuring they meet rigorous standards of quality, performance, and security
    accreditation for a classified deployment 
  - Work onsite in Washington D.C. to deploy Hazel onto classified networks

What We’re Looking For:

  - Proven experience as a full stack engineer or similar role 
  - Proven experience with the technologies in our Tech Stack, which includes:
      - Designing and implementing AWS cloud infrastructure 
      - Python 
      - Typescript 
      - React/Next.js  
      - PostgreSQL  
      - CI/CD tools (e.g., GitHub, CodePipeline) 
      - IaC (CDK/Terraform) 
      - Familiarity with Auth N/Auth Z/SAML/SSO/IdP 
      - Docker
  - Adeptness with using AI Coding Tools (e.g. Cursor/Claude Code) 
  - Willingness to spend 25% of time onsite with customers (all travel is covered) 
  - Excitement about bringing innovation to the public sector 
  - Continuous drive towards learning and personal development  
  - TS/SCI with FSP 
      - We will sponsor new clearances

Nice to Have Experience:

  - Has worked at a startup or startup-like environment 
  - Experience working in air-gapped or classified environments 
  - Security accreditation (e.g., IL-6, ICD-503) 
  - AWS Solutions Architect or similar 
  - Building or contributing to “from scratch” applications that had many users 
  - Mapping business priorities to technical priorities and vice versa 
  - Working with or adjacent to the public sector

Base Salary Range:

$150K - $200K USD | 0.25% - 0.75% Company Equity 

  - Estimate provided is dependent on a wide range of factors, including years of experience, relevant knowledge, and
    current security clearance 
  - Generous health & 401(k) benefits 
  - Relocation Assistance 
  - Unlimited PTO

Why Join Hazel:

This is Hazel’s first engagement in a new customer portfolio. We are one of the very first startups to ever win work
with this customer. You will lead this product deployment. If you are interested in a career in national security, we
will sponsor your Top Secret clearance for this role.

As a Hazel engineer, you’ll architect and deploy secure, scalable systems that bring AI to government procurement.
You’ll own features end-to-end, from backend services and data pipelines to model integration and front-end delivery,
helping our partners move faster and smarter. Hazel combines startup speed with the mission focus of public service.

You’ll work side-by-side with inquisitive and driven founders as well as a world-class and dynamic founding engineering
team. Hazel continuously promotes learning and provides numerous resources from our founders, other startups, and VCs –
as well as frontline exposure to customer executives and multiple engineering skillsets.

Hazel is a mission-driven organization founded by engineers and built around delivering world-class innovation to our
government partners. We strive for excellence, deliver impact, and have fun doing it.

How You Fit Us:

You care about mission. Hazel partners with agencies supporting everything from public school teachers in the classroom
to warfighters in the field. We believe in products which change America for the better. 

You want a startup that is structured without being rigid, quality-obsessed without being slow, and product-led without
losing the vision. You take ownership: shaping the roadmap, talking to customers, and wearing many hats. We build
exceptional generalists. 

You solve problems. There’s no more time to opine on strategy and policy when our nation faces existential challenges,
today. We are workhorses, not showhorses. 

You are always learning. Nobody has all the answers, and the world is ever-evolving, so we must be adaptive. We bring
the best practices available from all domains to meet the challenge. 

You believe in team. Our team grows together, supports one another, and elevates our shared successes. We are more
effective together.

Disclosures:

Hazel is an Equal Opportunity Employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without
regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability or veteran
status, age, or any other federally protected class.

Hazel’s name is inspired by Hazel Ying Lee, one of the first Chinese-American women to serve in the U.S. military as a
member of the Women Airforce Service Pilots in World War II. All Americans can break barriers, dare to innovate, and be
the change.

articles.title: Is One Layer Enough? A Single Transformer Layer Matches Full-Parameter RL Train
articles.originalTitle: Is One Layer Enough? A Single Transformer Layer Matches Full-Parameter RL Train
articles.excerpt: Reinforcement learning (RL) has become a central component of post-training large language models (LLMs), yet little is understood about how RL adaptation is distributed across transformer layers. Existing approaches typically update all model parameters uniformly, implicitly assuming that every layer contributes similarly to the gains obtained during RL post-training. In this work, we challenge this assumption through a systematic layer-wise study of RL training. Surprisingly, we find that training a single transformer layer can recover most of the gains achieved by full-parameter RL training, and in some cases even surpass it. To quantify this phenomenon, we introduce the quantity layer contribution, which measures the fraction of full RL improvement recovered by training a layer in isolation. Across seven models spanning two model families (Qwen3, Qwen2.5), three RL algorithms (GRPO, GiGPO, Dr. GRPO), and multiple task domains including mathematical reasoning, code generation, and agentic decision-making, we observe a remarkably stable pattern: RL gains are highly concentrated in a small subset of, and in many cases even a single, transformer layers. More strikingly, the same structural pattern consistently emerges: high-contribution layers concentrate in the middle of the transformer stack, while layers near the input and output ends contribute substantially less. The resulting layer rankings remain strongly correlated across datasets, tasks, model families, and RL algorithms.

articles.originalTitle: Pijani rodzice zaatakowali policjantów. 2-letnie dziecko trafiło do pogotowia opiekuńczego
articles.excerpt: Do dramatycznych scen doszło w jednym z bloków w Kołobrzegu (woj. zachodniopomorskie), gdzie policja została wezwana do awanturujących się rodziców dwuletniego chłopca. Zgłoszenie dotyczyło głośnej kłótni, która miała miejsce już na klatce schodowej. Na miejscu funkcjonariusze zastali przewrócony wózek dziecięcy oraz pijaną parę. 19-latka i 21-latek byli także agresywni wobec policjantów.
